SECTION IX - COORDINATION 
9.01 Public Notice. The United States Section of the International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC), on February 12, 1976 issued a public notice in connection with the proposed hydroelectric plant at the Rio Grande's Amistad Dam.
9.02 Public Meeting. A public meeting, sponsored by the IBWC, was held at 7:30 p.m. on July 1, 1976 at the Civic Center, Del Rio, Texas. The purpose of the meeting was to inform the public of the proposal to construct a hydroelectric power plant on the United States side at Amistad Dam and to obtain an expression of the public views and concerns. At the meeting, Mr. J. F. Friedkin, United States Commissioner of the International Boundary and Water Commission, presented the proposed plan of development. Public statements were made and entered into the public record. Questions were directed to Mr. Friedkin to clear up any public misconceptions concerning the proposed project. In general, the questions ranged from cost details to reasons for not installing hydroelectric generators during initial construction. The Maverick County Water Control Improvement District No. 1 expressed a desire to coordinate the releases at Amistad Dam with their power plant to effect maximum utilization of their plant. A total of 17 officials, residents, or interested citizens made statements or asked questions concerning the proposed action. A representative from Congressman Kreuger's office in San Antonio, Texas, offered the Congressman's assistance in any matter of the project.
9.03 Coordination of the Draft Environmental Statement. Future coordination activities, including comments received from individuals and agencies and the responses to those comments, will be included in the final environmental statement. 
9.04 Correspondence on Land Use Plans. Federal, state, and local governmental agencies were requested to evaluate the relationship of the proposed action on the Rio Grande to their respective land use plans. Their written correspondence is displayed in this section. Table IX-1 presents an index to facilitate locating the correspondence of a particular agency.
